name: Martensite
desc: A diffusionless military shear caught mid-avalanche: lenticular plates snap into the austenite along their habit planes at the speed of sound, each with a midrib and internal twins, each stopping dead where it strikes another plate, and because the strain at a plate tip triggers the next one they arrive in autocatalytic cascades that partition the parent grains hierarchically into ever finer self-accommodating wedges - then the specimen is cycled around its hysteresis loop and the plates reverse last-formed-first; read as an etched metallographic section, tint-etched variant colour, latent-heat thermal, or a blueprint of habit-plane traces.

energy.doc: etch contrast and the latent-heat flash as each plate snaps in

scale.doc: magnification into the section - guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: thermal cycling rate around the hysteresis loop, and how fast plates snap out (0.2 still cycles)

density.doc: peak transformed fraction and plate fineness - a few bold laths vs a dense fine-plate cascade

twin.doc: internal twin striation frequency and contrast across each plate

grain.doc: polishing scratches and etch tooth on the austenite

hue.doc: base hue; the four habit-plane variants fan out from it

x.doc: pan across the section when magnified

y.doc: pan down the section when magnified

style.doc: aesthetic: etched metallographic section / tint-etched variant colour / latent-heat ironbow thermal / blueprint of habit-plane traces

seed.doc: deterministic parent grains, variant orientations and nucleation
